newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HMOs' Q2 seen uneven, cost trends accelerate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HMOs' Q2 seen uneven, cost trends accelerate.

text.p: U.S. HMOs are still finding their footing after a difficult 1996, with second-quarter results expected to reflect the industry's struggle to rein in medical cost inflation and restore profit margins.
In coming weeks, health maintenance organizations will report varying year-over-year profit-and-loss comparisons, even as analysts point to more challenges in 1998.

"We are seeing evidence that (medical) cost trends are turning up and we expect that to pick up a little more in the second half of 1997 into 1998," said Peter Reilly, an actuary at Milliman & Robertson, a healthcare consulting firm.
Through the first half of 1997, HMO market leader United HealthCare Corp and others assured Wall Street that medical costs were climbing a steady three to four percent.

At the same time, HMOs had been able to hike premiums in the five-percent range during the key January enrollment period, indicating some movement toward improving medical loss ratios -- the key measure of HMO profitability, analysts said.
That equation may be strained in the future, however, as both premium and cost levels rise at faster rates, analysts said.

"Keeping the medical cost trend for the overall industry in this three to four percent range that people are talking about is going to be a difficult task," said Bear Stearns managed healthcare industry analyst Gary Frazier.
Along with higher costs, premiums look ready to increase in the four-to-seven percent range next year, analysts said.
"So you could see the industry getting itself positioned for a small degree of margin expansion in 1998. It's not going to be huge like we had in the early 1990s," Frazier said.

In 1996, HMOs were caught short by unexpected increases in medical cost inflation that outstripped premium hikes. The margin compression that resulted undercut profits and soured the market on HMOs, in general, although larger stocks have ridden 1997's broad blue-chip rally to new highs.

Up strongly this year are Aetna Inc, WellPoint Health Networks Inc Inc, United Wisconsin Services Inc and perennial powerhouse Oxford Health Plans Inc. Moderate gainers have included United HealthCare, Mid Atlantic Medical Services Inc and Humana Inc. Saddled with difficulties from a recent merger, PacifiCare Health Systems Inc continues to lag.
